C05-M01-L06-F1.title: The evidence lifecycle from capture to destruction
C05-M01-L06-F1.caption: Each item of evidence is captured, hashed, logged, stored, verified at every hand-off, retained only as agreed and then destroyed with a record.
C05-M01-L06-F1.alt: Top-to-bottom flow of seven steps: Capture (request, response, tool output, UTC time); Hash at capture (SHA-256 into the manifest); Log custody (who, when, where, why); Secure storage (encrypted, access-controlled, client-approved); Transfer and verify (recompute hash at every hand-off); Retain (only for the agreed period); Destroy and certify (sanitise, record, confirm to the client), the last step highlighted as the outcome.

steps.label: Capture
steps.sub: request, response, tool output, UTC time

steps.label: Destroy and certify
steps.sub: sanitise, record, confirm to the client

C05-M01-L06-F1.note: Skipping a stage weakens every later one: an item not hashed at capture can never be proved unaltered.

C05-M01-L06-F2.title: A custody hand-off verified by hash
C05-M01-L06-F2.caption: The receiver trusts evidence only when its recomputed SHA-256 matches a value recorded separately in the custody log.
C05-M01-L06-F2.alt: Sequence diagram with three lanes: Tester (captures and hashes), Custody log (separate record) and Reviewer (peer or client). Tester to Custody log: Record SHA-256 at capture. Tester to Reviewer: Evidence file + manifest. Reviewer to Custody log: Fetch recorded hash. Custody log to Reviewer, dashed: Expected SHA-256. Reviewer to Custody log: Log: received, hash OK (or FAILED). Reviewer to Tester, dashed: Acknowledge receipt.
C05-M01-L06-F2.note: A mismatch quarantines the item: it is not cited in the report until the change is explained.
